plan: My private value is $30. In a first-price sealed bid auction with two other bidders, I want to bid strategically. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. If I bid too high, I risk paying more than my value. If I bid too low, I might lose the auction. A reasonable strategy is to bid around $25-$28 - close to my value but with some profit margin built in.

My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to minimize overpaying. I'll aim to win by bidding just enough to beat competitors, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. A bid around $32-$33 seems strategic - close to my value but with a buffer against potential losses.

With a private value of $6, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the winning strategy depends on anticipating other bidders' behavior, I'll aim to bid slightly above my value but not excessively. Given the random nature and single round, I'll bid close to my value but with a modest markup to increase winning chances.
